text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today as U.S. crude oil dropped nearly 8% for the week following diplomatic talks between Iran and the U.S. at the United Nations. When oil prices weaken—crude is now at $96.41 per barrel, down from higher levels earlier in the week—it directly reduces the value of oil company earnings and cash flow, which is the core driver of their stock prices.

The broader context is a shift in market risk sentiment: news of potential nuclear talks and Iran's willingness to reopen the Strait of Hormuz (a critical oil chokepoint) has eased supply-shock fears that had been supporting oil prices. At the same time, Saudi Arabia is ramping up exports despite regional tensions, signaling more oil coming to market rather than less. That combination—less geopolitical tension risk plus rising supply—removes the premium that had been built into energy stocks over the past two weeks.
